newsitem.title: FRANCE: French agents chief give "qualified" support for Air Canada initiative.
newsitem.headline: French agents chief give "qualified" support for Air Canada initiative.

text.p: French air cargo agents association president, Klaus Pfab, has expressed "qualified" support for Air Canada's initiative in introducing financial penalties against forwarders or shippers who fail to use pre-booked space.

"We are basically in favour of measures which promote transparency and discipline in the sector. However, this is a two-way process, with airlines having their part to play too, for example, giving shipment guarantees to customers who have booked space," Pfab said.

He added: "There have been numerous instances where airlines have put aside "booked" freight at the last minute in the interests of yield management as more "lucrative" freight has come in at short notice. This practice is every bit as objectionable as a no-show."
Air Canada has decided to impose fines equal to 50 percent of the booked weight at the applicable tariffs, effective March 1.

The fines will be invoiced through the industry's cargo account settlement system (CASS) against forwarders and shippers who fail to use pre-booked capacity on weekend flights from Europe. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
